2607.21804.title: Adversarial Prompts for Acceptance Collapse in Speculative Decoding
2607.21804.paper_summary: Lossless acceleration schemes, such as speculative decoding, promise significant inference speedups by relying on dynamic token-level alignment between a draft and a target model. However, this guarantee of semantic equivalence masks a severe operational vulnerability: draft-target alignment can be systematically attacked. In this paper, we introduce ADSD, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first prompt-suffix attack that collapses verifier acceptance by pushing draft probability mass toward tokens the target is unlikely to accept. ADSD uses Soft-Collapse, a verifier-aligned surrogate derived from the asymmetric speculative acceptance rule, together with a target-preservation objective that discourages obvious task corruption. ADSD successfully generates highly effective adversarial suffixes. On the GSM8K dataset, our attack increases the mean sample time by 62.3% while preserving the task quality. We further show that this vulnerability exists across different domains, speculative decoding strategies, and model architectures.
2607.21804.paper_summary_zh: 無損加速方案，例如推測解碼，通過依賴草稿模型與目標模型之間的動態標記級對齊，承諾顯著的推斷速度提升。然而，這種語義等價的保證掩蓋了一個嚴重的操作脆弱性：草稿與目標的對齊可以被系統性地攻擊。在本文中，我們介紹了ADSD，據我們所知，這是第一個通過將草稿概率質量推向目標不太可能接受的標記來崩潰驗證器接受的提示後綴攻擊。ADSD使用Soft-Collapse，這是一種基於非對稱推測接受規則的驗證器對齊代理，並結合了一個目標保護目標，以防止明顯的任務腐敗。ADSD成功生成了高效的對抗後綴。在GSM8K數據集上，我們的攻擊將平均樣本時間提高了62.3%，同時保持了任務質量。我們進一步表明，這一脆弱性存在於不同的領域、推測解碼策略和模型架構中。
